rows.claim: Tracer docstring (tracer.jl:19-26) says the global tracer throws Undecidable on a value-severing conversion 'touching a tagged operand'; the code throws on any Tracer{true}, tagged or not
rows.evidence: src/tracer.jl:49 Base.Float64(::Tracer{true}) = throw(Undecidable()); probe:12 Float64 of an untagged Tracer{true} throws Undecidable, while probe:13 an untagged comparison passes (src/tracer.jl:103 _decide). So a Float64() of a state, mode or parameter value in stage 2 forces the sampled fallback, against spec.md:12403 'branching on state, modes, parameters or time never interferes'
rows.fix: Code: Base.Float64(x::Tracer{S}) where {S} = (_decide(S, x.dependencies); x.value), so only a tainted conversion refuses. If the blanket refusal is intended, change the docstring to 'a value-severing conversion of any global-tracer value' and add the rule to spec §13.8.

rows.claim: LoopError docstring says a run ends with it 'when a frame throws, whatever it throws', that the throw leaves the simulation errored, and that exception is a wrapper whose cause is the raw error; a fault outside the frame ends stopped and holds the raw exception (run! docstring, sim.jl:1514, repeats it)
rows.evidence: test/test_lattices.jl:392-409 an unbounded run! ends :stopped with sim.model.status :consistent and a LoopError whose exception is DiagnosticError{ArgumentInvalid}, not a StepError; src/sim.jl:1757 LoopError(cause) on any cause; design/spec.md:11906-11915 states both cases (D-317, D-445, D-450)
rows.fix: LoopError docstring: 'A failure inside a frame leaves the simulation `errored`, and `exception` is the `StepError` that wraps the raw error or the failed check's diagnostic as `cause`. A fault outside a frame, such as the refusal of a frame past the last the run may take, leaves it `stopped` with `exception` the raw throw.' Give run!'s sentence the same split.

rows.claim: Each advance reads an honoured stop request off the latest snapshot before it reads the pending control stop word; with both holding, the record names ModelRequestedStop, whereas spec §13.5's fixed order puts the control stop first
rows.evidence: src/sim.jl:2090-2091 _stop_hit returns before the loop's `issuer` read at 2099-2100; probe:44-47 stop!(sim) then step!(sim) with a request holding at boundary zero gives 0 frames and ModelRequestedStop("s", :y, "x"), probe:54 the same without a request gives ControlRequestedStop(:code); design/spec.md:11859-11863 'checks a pending control stop at frame top, then t_end, then the stop requests'; D-413 records the entry check but not its place in the order; step! docstring says a stop issued before the call 'ends that call at once' with 0 frames
rows.fix: Spec §13.5, 'The scan and the source order': 'The entry check of the latest snapshot for an honoured request comes before the pending control stop, so a request holding at entry is named even beside a pending stop.' Or, if the order is meant to hold, a code change: move the entry `_stop_hit` after the `stop_issuer` read in _advance!.

rows.claim: step! docstring says frames is 'an integer of at least 1 that keeps the frame index within Int'; the code bounds it by the last frame the run may take, which can be far below typemax(Int)
rows.evidence: src/sim.jl:2229 `1 ≤ frame_count ≤ _last_frame(sim.model) - sim.run.frame`; test/test_lattices.jl:389-390 step!(sim; frames = 1001) refused on a model whose last frame is 1000; the t_plus bullet and run!'s t_end bullet already say 'within the frame range'
rows.fix: `frames`: the number of frames to advance, an integer of at least 1 within the frame range, so that the frame index stays at or below the last frame the run may take.
